definition_zh: 卑劣之徒；懦夫（古旧用法）
definition_en: a base, cowardly or despicable person (archaic); as an adjective, cowardly and mean
core_image: 黑暗巷口畏缩着递出勒索信的无耻小人
scene: 旧戏台上，恶仆缩在柱后偷听主人说话。The caitiff fled as soon as the guards appeared.
sceneCN: 这里 caitiff 是「卑劣的懦夫」（第 1 个义项：可鄙而怯懦之人）；句意是卫兵一现身，这无耻之徒立刻逃窜。

pos.zh: 卑劣之徒；懦夫；可鄙的人

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「囚禁；被俘」
同根动词，义为「俘获（人心）；迷住」
同根名词，义为「俘虏；囚徒」

senses.title: A base or cowardly person
senses.definition: a despicable, cowardly person, especially a villain of low character
senses.definitionCN: 可鄙而怯懦之人，尤指品性低劣的恶徒
senses.example: The caitiff betrayed his master for a purse of coin.
senses.exampleCN: 这卑劣之徒为了一袋金币出卖了主人。
senses.why: The word began as captive, one taken, and slid to one too base to fight.
senses.whyCN: 此词本义「被俘者」，渐转指不敢一战的无耻之辈。

senses.title: Cowardly and base (adjective)
senses.definition: mean, cowardly, or despicable in character or action
senses.definitionCN: 品性或行为卑劣、怯懦、可鄙
senses.example: It was a caitiff trick to poison a guest.
senses.exampleCN: 毒害宾客是卑劣的伎俩。
senses.why: The noun of the wretch becomes the adjective of his deeds.
senses.whyCN: 由「卑劣者」之名转为「卑劣」之形容。

intro.en: Caitiff descends from Latin captivus, a prisoner, through Old French caitif, drifting from captive to coward.
intro.cn: caitiff 源自拉丁语 captivus（俘虏），经古法语 caitif，由「被俘者」渐转「卑怯者」。

items.en: behind Latin capere lies a reconstructed root kap-, to take or seize, uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 背后是表「抓取」的重构词根 kap-，细节不确定。

items.en: capere meant to take; captivus meant a taken one, a prisoner.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为「抓取」，captivus 即「被拿获者」，俘虏。

items.en: caitif meant wretched, a poor prisoner or miserable person.
items.cn: 古法语 caitif 意为「悲惨的」，指可怜的囚徒或不幸者。

items.en: caitif meant wretched or captive, then a base scoundrel.
items.cn: 中古英语 caitif 先指「悲惨的、被俘的」，后指卑劣恶徒。

items.en: caitiff survives as an archaic, literary insult.
items.cn: 如今 caitiff 是古雅的文学骂语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the seizing root; the near-meaning group lists scoundrel words.
note.cn: 形近组同出「抓取」词根；近义组是恶徒类词。

entries.definition: the state of being held prisoner

entries.definitionCN: 阳离子，仅拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a wicked person in a story or deed

normalIntro.en: From prisoner to poltroon: the word's history is itself a fall.
normalIntro.cn: 从俘虏到懦夫：这个词的历史本身就是一次堕落。

normal.cn: 拉丁语 captivus 意为俘虏。
古法语 caitif 意为悲惨的。
caitiff 本义只是「不幸的、可怜的」。

normal.en: Caitiff is now an archaic literary insult.
normal.cn: caitiff 现为古旧的文学骂语。

abstract.en: See a hooded figure scuttle away in the dark.
abstract.cn: 看一个兜帽身影在黑暗中仓皇逃窜。

abstract.en: Hear chains rattle in an old dungeon.
Feel the contempt in an old knight's voice.
abstract.cn: 感受老骑士话音中的鄙夷。

examples.en: Back, caitiff, and face your debt!
examples.cn: 退后，卑劣之徒，来面对你的债！

examples.en: The novel's caitiff steward robs the estate piece by piece.
examples.cn: 小说里卑劣的管家把庄园一点点偷空。

examples.en: Such caitiff excuses fool no one.
examples.cn: 如此卑劣的借口骗不了任何人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开·踢夫」——懦夫只想开溜，被人追着踢，狼狈不堪。

root: caitiff 源自拉丁语 captivus「俘虏」（capere「抓取」的派生词），经古法语 caitif「悲惨者」进入英语；词义由「被俘的可怜人」滑向「卑怯的无耻之徒」；同族词 captive、captivity、captivate 保留「抓取」本义。

sensesIntro.en: Once the wretched prisoner, the word turned on those too base to stand and fight.
sensesIntro.cn: 它原指可怜的囚徒，后来转骂那些卑怯到不敢挺身一战之人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cringing figure in a dark alley.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗巷里畏缩的身影。

branches.en: a caitiff who betrays for coin
the caitiff flees at the first guard
the wretch and his wretched deeds

intro.en: Caitiff wears the same -ive family ending as captive, worn smooth by French mouths.
intro.cn: caitiff 与 captive 共用 -ive 词族词尾，经法语口传而磨损。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere, to take, generates the whole seizing family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere「抓取」生出整个「抓取」词族。
